learning_objective: 🎯 Experience the vibrant beauty of nature! Learn how the poet uses vivid imagery to capture the elusive and majestic presence of India's national bird.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The poem captures the feeling of trying to spot a peacock. It is rarely seen fully at first; instead, you catch a flash of turquoise or the darting of its tail. Its beauty is magnified by its elusive nature.
The speaker is reading a book, but the subtle sounds of the peacock (a blue shadow, the wind changing) break her concentration. It shows how nature’s magnetic presence overpowers human activities.
The mention of the 'pipal' tree firmly roots the poem in the Indian landscape. The peacock is not just a bird; it represents the vibrant, wild essence of India.

When the peacock finally reveals itself, gathering its tail to drop from the tree, it is a moment of breathtaking awe. The poet compares its eyes (on the feathers) to something that seems to 'blink' as it descends.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 Color Palette Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: The poet uses colors like 'turquoise' to describe the bird. Look around your room and find three objects that perfectly match the vibrant blue-green of a peacock's feather. It's harder than you think!

exam_tips: 📌 Imagery is the most important literary device here. The poet uses visual (turquoise, blue shadow) and auditory (wind in the pipal tree) imagery to make you 'feel' the bird's presence.
📌 Explain why the poet mentions reading a book: it creates a contrast between the static, intellectual world of books and the dynamic, captivating world of nature.
📌 The phrase 'eyes blinking' refers to the eye-like patterns on the peacock's tail feathers catching the light as it moves.
quick_recap: ⭐ The poem is written in free verse, which mimics the natural, unpredictable movement of the peacock.
⭐ The peacock is a symbol of wild, untamed beauty that demands attention.
⭐ Sujata Bhatt effectively captures the suspense of 'waiting' to see the bird fully.
